historical_record.description: The Stadium, designed by A. B. Spreckels and John McLaren, was an oval of thirty acres east of Thirty-sixth Avenue ringed by a sixty-foot trotting track, with a bicycle track, cinder tracks and room for six football fields inside, a grassy terrace for 60,000 spectators, and tunnels under the track on the north and south; a grandstand then being built would bring the seating to 100,000.
